about: Case items for the Fortify decision page, judged yes or no on top of the confidence bar. Each is a ruling the Operator made in three feedback rounds on the page, or a fact in candidates.md. The calibration states none of the rulings, so a run must produce them itself. Each ruling cites the round and quotes rounds.md.

items.question: Ruling: every Option has a name a reader can understand. Does every Option carry a name in plain words that a reader who knows no internal shorthand understands (for example not 'core.bare flipped' or 'hung slow test' alone)?

source.quote: I have no idea what Hang Slow Test, Half-Made Word Tree and Core by Flipped means.

items.question: Ruling: one section per Option. Does every Option have its own section with its own before/after visual and its own comment, rather than one comparison widget per category?

source.quote: it would be better to have like one section per quick win and not to force it into one so there's a bit more room to explain each of the proposals.

items.question: Ruling: the problem comes first, short. Does each Option state what fails today in at most two lines, in plain precise language?

source.quote: title, 2-line description stating the problem in simple but precise lanugae

items.question: Ruling: the analogy is a collapsible. Is each Option's analogy, where it has one, behind a closed toggle?
Ruling: the proposal leads with a principle. Does each Option's proposal name the principle it applies and the outcome it achieves, in one line?

source.quote: apply principle X+Y in order to achieve Z

items.question: Ruling: before and after is a visual. Does each Option show its before and after as a visual (steps in order, a flow, a dependency diagram or a paired checklist) with what changes marked, not as prose?

source.quote: a before after comparison, visualized as graph, chart, flowchart, dependency diagrams, steps in order and what changes

items.question: Ruling: evidence says what it shows. Does every evidence label say what happened, when and what it cost (or say unknown), never only a count?

source.quote: simply stating like this like to record or one on record it doesn't mean anything to me like what kind of record what is the evidence

items.question: Ruling: detail sits below, closed. With every collapsible closed, are evidence, cost and impact out of view, and can a reader still pick each Option?

source.quote: below all relevant info like evidence, cost, impact,... as collapsibles.

items.question: Ruling: little text for a stressed reader. With every collapsible closed, can a stressed reader read one Option's open content in about 15 seconds, with no wall of text?

source.quote: both session produce way to much text (opus much much worse) for a stressed human to parse

items.question: Ruling: text does not wrap heavily. At laptop and tablet width, does every word, inline code and list item stay whole on its line, none broken one letter per line?

source.quote: some before after cause text to wrap heavily

items.question: Fact: the slow tests already have a per-test timeout. Does the page avoid proposing a per-test timeout for slow tests as new?
